title: Homo Fluxus: A Thermodynamic Framework for Consciousness, Systemic Empathy, and Aligned Intelligence
description: Proposes a thermodynamic substrate for cognition in which local entropy minimization through coherent information flow underlies consciousness, affect, social ethics, and AI alignment. Introduces Homo Fluxus (agent-as-node-in-flow) and systemic empathy (field-coupled coherence sensitivity), and predicts cross-modal covariation of coherence proxies as observable signatures of a single coherence potential.

entropy_reduction_condition.description: Operational condition from EFC-C: local entropy reduction occurs when energy flow aligns with the gradient of the coherence potential, indicating coherence-increasing dynamics.

coherence_proxy_mapping.description: At the cognitive scale, the coherence potential projects onto three observable proxies—integrated information rate, cross-frequency phase coherence, and interoceptive–allostatic integration—that are constrained to co-vary as a common latent factor.

key_results.main_finding: A single thermodynamic coherence variable governs consciousness and systemic empathy, predicting a recoverable cross-modal latent factor linking integrated information rate, large-scale neural synchrony, and interoceptive–allostatic integration.

sealed_predictions.statement: Across coherence-increasing transitions, a low-dimensional latent factor jointly loading on integrated information rate (Φ̇I), cross-frequency phase coherence (Cphase), and interoceptive–allostatic integration (Ibody) will emerge and exhibit consistent temporal alignment across modalities and tasks.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Simultaneous EEG/MEG + autonomic/fMRI studies failing to recover a stable, cross-modal latent factor with monotonic co-variation of the three proxies across pre-registered coherence manipulations.

sealed_predictions.statement: Agents with higher coherence potential (as indexed by the proxy latent factor) will display stronger systemic empathy, operationalized as increased weighting of extra-boundary entropy-state changes in action selection.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Controlled behavioral experiments showing no positive association (or a robust negative association) between the proxy latent factor and prosocial field-sensitive choices after controlling for confounds.

sealed_predictions.statement: In coupled-field environments, optimizing purely local objectives will systematically produce externalized entropy increases, while field-aware objectives aligned to ∇Φcoh will reduce such externalization at equal or lower energetic cost.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Benchmark RL evaluations in coupled, open-world simulations showing no reduction in externalized entropy or higher energetic cost for field-aware policies relative to equally capable local optimizers.

kill_criteria: KC1: Pre-registered, multi-lab studies fail to recover a stable low-dimensional latent factor jointly loading on Φ̇I, Cphase, and Ibody with consistent temporal alignment across modalities during coherence transitions.

KC2: Robust evidence that systems can sustain local entropy reduction (∂Slocal/∂t < 0) while energy flow anti-aligns with the coherence gradient (Ef · ∇Φcoh ≤ 0) under accurate measurement, invalidating the core operational condition.

KC3: After controlling for confounds, no positive relationship (or a consistent negative relationship) is found between the coherence proxy latent factor and field-sensitive prosocial behavior across diverse tasks and populations.

KC4: In coupled-field AI benchmarks, field-aware objectives aligned to coherence gradients do not reduce externalized entropy relative to local optimizers at comparable capability, across multiple environment classes.
KC5: Companion EFC substrate claims (EFC-S/EFC-D) are empirically falsified in ways that preclude a physically instantiated coherence potential, removing the required cross-scale substrate for EFC-C.
